title: Console gated surface minimization: reduce heavy tiles for initial rollout
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description:
Summary: For the initial Console observability rollout we will intentionally reduce the surface area and gate higher-cost, high-cardinality experiences behind feature flags. This ticket documents concrete scope reductions across dashboards, tracing, and cost breakdown so the team can ship a robust, low-cost MVP while retaining hooks for phased re-enablement.

Context: Telemetry sampling, multi-dimension cost breakdowns, and per-token trace timelines add significant backend and UI complexity. Early telemetry shows these features could double query costs and complicate rollout stability. The goal is to deliver core usefulness (route-level latency, error rates, coarse cost trends) without shipping expensive exploratory tooling until we have batching, trace-caching, and query quotas in place.

Out of scope: Long-term high-cardinality filters, deep trace flamegraphs, and live streaming trace navigation for the MVP. Those will be delivered by follow-on epics once autoscaling and cache recommendations land.
acceptance_criteria: A1: Default Console landing shows 3 compact tiles (Route Vitals, 7-day Cost Trend, Error Rates) — no more than 3 backend queries at load
A2: Tracing pane available but starts in 'Sampled Summary' mode (top-3 traces by latency) and links into an off-by-default detailed trace explorer gated by feature flag 'trace_deep_inspect'
A3: Cost breakdown card displays aggregated cost per route and a single percent-change sparkline; multi-dimension breakdown (region/model/deployment) behind feature flag 'cost_breakdown_deep'
A4: All gated features default to OFF for new tenants and can be toggled per-org in Console settings
A5: Backend rate/compute budget for the MVP enforced: any single UI load cannot trigger more than 5 heavy DB/telemetry queries; automated tests validate this budget
A6: UX fallback flows implemented: when a gated feature is toggled off the UI shows a clear CTA linking to docs and a request access form
A7: Shipping checklist includes load test demonstrating <20% additional CPU at typical org scale and cost delta estimate in billing dashboard for beta customers
decisions: D1: Prioritize route-level observability and coarse cost signals over exploratory high-cardinality tooling for initial public rollout
D2: Implement feature flags for all interfaces that require additional telemetry or heavy queries; flags default to off for security/cost reasons
D3: Reuse existing runtime KV prefix cache for trace timeline aggregation to reduce per-load query counts rather than building a separate trace cache in MVP
tradeoffs: T1: Reduced diagnostic depth may increase time-to-resolution for customers with complex incidents until detailed tracing is enabled
T2: Gating features increases administrative overhead (feature flag config and QA permutations) but lowers risk of runaway costs
T3: Simpler cost card reduces immediate insights for power users but enables faster shipping and lower infra spend
